correctness.rationale: The gradient step is A=a uuᵀ or B=b vvᵀ (a,b∈(0,1)); direct products give RR Gram =a²b²c²/2 (uuᵀ+vvᵀ) and IID Gram=1/4[(a⁴+a²b²c²)uuᵀ+(b⁴+a²b²c²)vvᵀ]. Since u,v are independent, x↦(uᵀx,vᵀx) is invertible and IID−RR is PSD iff a≥bc and b≥ac. Above boundary the two coefficients have opposite signs, proving true directional reversal. The bisector maximizes RR Gram; IID−RR evaluated there is (1+c)(a⁴+b⁴−2a²b²c²)/8>0, yielding strict worst-case improvement. IID = RR/2 + (a⁴(uᵀx)²+b⁴(vᵀx)²)/4 gives RR<2 IID for all nonzero x, sharp as a→0 along x⊥v. Exact rational witness a=1/4,b=3/4,c=3/5,x=(-4/5,3/5) yields RR=81/20000 versus IID=53/20000; independently checked. All continuous quantifiers follow from the exact Gram argument, not the tests.
